rationale: Publisher PDF and official meeting member Section RPS 1403a-7 on PDF page 540 records Beller's habitual coffee assessment in 300 adults without cardiovascular disease. Higher consumption tracked with some MRI cardiac-function parameters. Brain small-vessel imaging measures showed no clear association. The study grouped all coffee and reports no fatigue comparison or Parkinson subgroup. Elsewhere in the book, Coffee & Talk labels mark conference events. The Parkinson imaging and other fatigue members address different cohorts.

Publisher PDF and official meeting member The volume uses date in scheduling and clinical chronology. A second text mapping was screened for dates, date palm, Phoenix dactylifera and dried fruit. No member connects dried date intake to Parkinson pain. The genuine coffee member addresses cardiovascular imaging.

Parkinson causation review Figure 1 uses orange as a display color for nongenetic factors in its schematic. The review explains causal inference and does not assign raw orange or measure food-associated fall frequency.
Historical brain drug delivery review Figures 9 and 18 use orange for a membrane region and pseudocolored astrocytes. The drug delivery examples contain no raw fruit comparison for Parkinson falls.

Systematic review of backward walking and cognition in Parkinson disease Orange Labs appears as an affiliation. The reviewed exposures involve walking or tasks and their cognitive correlates. The source contains no raw orange fall-frequency estimate.

Nonhuman experiment on a mushroom glycoprotein The experimental comparison concerns a mushroom-derived glycoprotein and lead-associated liver injury in rats. No orange intake or Parkinson fall measure was assessed.

Cissus tuberosa laboratory study and linked citrus citation The Cissus experiment studies a separate plant extract. Its discussion and reference 53 cite Hamed's Citrus sinensis peel-extract study in a rat model. The cited peel exposure is a related orange product. Neither report supplies a raw fruit comparison or clinical fall frequency.

Human HLA fine-mapping case-control analysis in Alzheimer disease EGG occurs in the author-contribution initials. The study evaluates HLA associations with Alzheimer disease and has no poached egg exposure or Parkinson fall-frequency comparison.

Tourette syndrome quality-of-life review The authors review tic-related functional impairment, comorbidities and quality-of-life instruments. Pain is an instrument domain or an item in Tourette symptom context. Parkinson disease appears in separate instrument-development context. No dried date or dietary pain comparison appears.

Robot-assisted gait training pilot Training and mobility or psychosocial outcomes define the comparison. No dried date intake was measured or assigned, so the pilot supplies no date-associated Parkinson pain estimate.

Hospital readmission analysis in stiff person syndrome The design uses administrative hospitalization and readmission timing in stiff person syndrome. Admission timing is distinct from a dietary date exposure. The results do not compare dried date and Parkinson pain.

Cross-sectional study of Parkinson sleep and restless legs The analysis estimates the association of probable REM sleep behavior disorder with restless legs in Parkinson disease. It has no measured dried date intake or separate diet-associated pain outcome.

UK Biobank heartbeat complexity cohort The exposure is a heartbeat complexity measure and the outcomes are all-cause or cardiorespiratory mortality. The outcome tables cannot provide a dried date comparison for Parkinson pain.

Parkinson deep brain stimulation motor outcome prediction The study uses microelectrode recordings at implantation to predict outcomes following stimulation. The predictors and clinical outcomes do not include dried date intake or a food-associated pain contrast.
Study of colorectal cancer perioperative outcomes Heart failure and comorbidity are the risk exposures in a surgical cohort. No dried date intake or Parkinson pain outcome is evaluated.

Scoping review of social support in community gym participation The intervention strategies are social and practical supports for disability exercise participation. No date fruit pain comparison was reported in those scopes.

EJS ACT-PD treatment selection and trial platform prioritization The article describes how candidates were identified and prioritized. The paper supplies no assigned dried date or measured Parkinson pain comparison.
Blood biomarker comparison in Parkinson disease and glioma The study examines marker levels in clinical groups. Its comparisons contain no dried date exposure or effect on Parkinson pain.

Pharmacological dementia review Sections 9 and 10 address dementia with parkinsonism and medication evidence. Anxiety is described clinically and in medication results. Salmon is a surname in the references. No poached salmon exposure or salmon-associated Parkinson anxiety comparison appears.

Review of cognitive and physical interventions in metal dysfunction and neurodegeneration The main comparisons involve exercise or cognitive intervention and the review discusses associated behavioral outcomes. No dried date intake or attributable Parkinson apathy comparison appears.

Qualitative study of Parkinson carer support needs The study gathers interviews about support over disease stages. SAGE is the publishing context. Falls or mobility needs do not create a ground sage exposure.

Work-oriented health care program report The clinical program addresses employment as a treatment goal. SAGE is publisher metadata. Ground sage and changes in Parkinson fall frequency were not studied.

Review of digital approaches to Parkinson clinical trials The source discusses digital trial assessment and implementation. The SAGE text is publisher metadata. The review contains no culinary sage and fall-frequency comparison.

Scoping review of impulsive-compulsive behaviors under dopaminergic treatment The included risk factors and treatments concern behavior and pharmacological management. SAGE is the publisher. No ground sage exposure is linked to fall frequency.
Preclinical imaging study The study compares imaging markers in preclinical material. SAGE occurs in the publication context. No dietary ground sage exposure or clinical fall count appears.

Qualitative inquiry into clinical cognitive assessment in Parkinson disease The inquiry evaluates barriers and facilitators in care pathways. SAGE appears in publisher details. Neither the exposure nor the endpoint constitutes a ground sage and fall-frequency comparison.

Automatic sleep staging and atonia detection study The study assesses a sleep-signal method in REM sleep behavior disorder. SAGE is publication metadata. No ground sage intake or measured dietary fall frequency is reported.

Review of lycopene and cardiovascular outcomes The food-source discussion highlights tomato and other sources of lycopene. The source does not identify raw culinary bell pepper as a measured intervention or provide a bell-pepper fatigue estimate. A generic carotenoid context does not identify the frozen pepper exposure.

Review of Parkinson-related proteins and ischemic secondary injury SAGE occurs in publishing information. The subject is brain injury following ischemia. No fresh sage intake or corresponding fatigue effect in Parkinson disease was tested.

Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation review The paper describes mitochondrial structures, bioenergetics and disease mechanisms. It does not assess intake of ground saffron or report Parkinson fall counts under a food exposure.
